text: yeah, now i think, to be honest, because the game movement and jumping feels exactly like css bhop before zblock hit (which is intentional) we should treat the collision as a force that would push back against the player, and therefore would let you get faster movement through a hallway for example because you hold down space and so your just hitting the head against it and getting all the velocity. lol could be fun xD
resolution: Fixed the head-into-ceiling glitch and shaped it to the user's CSS-bhop feel. Jumping under a floor/roof/deck placed overhead made the player's head poke into the piece's solid band; the physics step had no vertical (head-bonk) response, so collideSolidRects treated the overlap as a horizontal intrusion and side-pushed the player around (the glitchy jitter). A ceiling is a surface whose normal points down, so the correct response removes only the velocity component INTO it (the upward part) and keeps horizontal momentum. Added ceilingUndersideAt() (framework/game/physics.zig) which finds the lowest solid-rect underside, finite-floor band only — walls have none, with the body column inside the footprint, axis-aligned and oriented rects alike; step() clamps the head just below it and zeroes rising velocity BEFORE collideSolidRects so the band overlap is gone and the horizontal push never fires on a ceiling. pvx/pvz are deliberately preserved per the user's request — you skim a low hallway at full speed (Source-style head-skim, bhop-feel) instead of being shoved to a stop. Added deterministic test 'head bonk: jumping into a ceiling caps the head and keeps horizontal speed' asserting the head never punches through, rising velocity zeroed at contact, and +x speed survives. no-V8 world_loader builds clean; game-physics 40/41 (the one red, hollow-ramp-slab rect step-up surface_speed, predates this work).
